summary: Building the deployment software that installs, updates and keeps Honeywell's edge Kubernetes platform running.
description: Root-caused a production incident where an idle appliance was running the exact same code as a healthy twin: the platform's own watchdog was restarting MicroK8s in a way that re-corrupted its network state, then restarting it again once the corruption came back. Closed the loop with image pre-caching, a non-rolling registry deploy, and a circuit breaker that halts auto-remediation after 5 escalations in 24 hours without disabling detection.

Measured a 32.5% cut in incremental-update install time (90m11s to 60m51s on a representative 44-package run) after finding that a fixed per-sequence datastore-drain pause, not any single package's install script, was the largest cost, then right-sized the pause and parallelized decompression and package installs.

Built the storage bootstrap logic that lets a node join with or without Ceph already healthy. If Ceph is up, ceph-csi becomes the default storage class immediately; otherwise PVCs land on hostpath storage and migrate later through a scale-down, copy, switch, scale-up sequence, since recreating a PVC directly on Ceph would lose data.

Implemented 2-node and N-node Pacemaker/Corosync failover for the cluster's floating VIP, including a 5-phase failover test that runs pre-flight, soft, hard, restore and verify checks in sequence, simulating a network partition and diffing data on the new primary before calling the test passed.

Built EdgeOrchestrator, the Go service exposing the appliance's REST/WebSocket control-plane API, which shells out to Ansible for cluster deploy and upgrade through argument-array exec calls rather than a shell, and tracks its own binary replacement across a self-update restart with a marker file so a crashed update can't be reported as a false success.

Built ForgeLinkLite, a cross-platform Go agent handling Azure IoT Hub provisioning and AMQP-over-WebSocket connectivity with certificate auth, backed by a KeePass credential vault and an active/passive handshake for HA failover.

summary: Built services across ForgeML's 8-microservice MLOps platform, and the pipeline that migrates and AI-translates SkySpark automation rules into Forge.
description: Built the model deployment engine that routes to Databricks Serving, AKS or edge devices from one API, using discriminated-union request types so each target's config gets validated at the boundary. A dual async loop then polls serving endpoints every 30 seconds and liveness every 5 minutes, with one loop's failure isolated from the other.

Routed model registrations through five security scanners covering SAST, dependency and license risk, container images, and AI-model artifacts, all behind one Strategy Pattern interface, so adding a new scanner meant writing a new class instead of another conditional.

Fine-tuned Gemini on Vertex AI to translate SkySpark's Axon rule language into Honeywell's Forge DSL, building the versioned prompt store and a tuning-job state machine that moves each job from queued to processing to succeeded or failed, tracking the resulting endpoint for later translation requests.

Built the asyncio event processor that consumes Azure Event Hub in real time, dispatches each event to one of three parsers behind a Factory Pattern, and writes the result to PostgreSQL and Unity Catalog concurrently with Blob Storage checkpointing for exactly-once delivery across restarts.

Built the service that migrates SkySpark building-automation rules into Forge: authenticating over SCRAM, parsing the Zinc and Trio formats SkySpark returns, and writing to PostgreSQL and Unity Catalog in parallel instead of sequentially, cutting write time roughly in half.
Wrote the BDD acceptance suite in Behave, covering 50+ scenarios across six workflow domains and running in parallel per tenant, plus Locust load tests spanning onboarding through deployment.

summary: Built the Databricks pipelines behind field service analytics, and the agent, memory and guardrail layers behind the Maintenance Assist chatbot.
description: Built 15+ PySpark ingestion pipelines on Databricks, pulling from 12+ source systems including SQL Server, Salesforce, SharePoint and several field-service databases into Delta Lake, using timestamp-based watermarking for incremental loads.

Engineered a Spark Structured Streaming pipeline over PDFs landing in Blob Storage with SCD Type 2 upserts so document changes stayed traceable across micro-batches, then wired Change Data Feed on the resulting Delta tables so vectorization jobs fired on each insert, update or delete instead of on a schedule.

Built the agent executor behind the Maintenance Assist chatbot, handling tool selection, chat history, topic generation and summarization through a YAML-driven config so each tenant's agent could run its own LLM, tools and prompts without a code change.

Added a guardrail layer that runs input and output safety checks in parallel with the LLM call, able to cancel an in-flight streamed response mid-generation if a violation surfaced, on top of an SSE streaming layer built to hold 100+ concurrent sessions.

Replaced plain sequential chat history with a PGVector-backed memory store that retrieves prior turns by similarity instead of recency, so the model's context window carried what was actually relevant to the current question.

Built the document vectorization pipeline feeding PGVector from tens of thousands of knowledge-base articles and service cases, plus an evaluation harness that scored chatbot answers with Azure OpenAI as an LLM judge across a 1,000+ question set.
